passages.scripture: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.

lines.text: God justifies us through faith.
We now have peace with God.
Jesus Christ is our Lord.
God gives us peace through Jesus Christ.
We have faith in Jesus Christ.
Through Jesus Christ, we have access to God's grace.
We stand in this grace by faith.
We rejoice because we hope for God's glory.

passages.scripture: Not only that, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.

lines.text: No only do we rejoice in the hope of Glory.
We also rejoice in our sufferings.
We know that suffering produces perseverance.
Perseverance produces character.
Character produces hope.

passages.scripture: And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us.

lines.text: God gives us His love.
God pours His love into our hearts.
God pours His love through the Holy Spirit.
God has given the Holy Spirit to us.
Our hope will not disappoint us.
What we hope for, what God has promised, we will receive.
We will not be disappointed that we hoped but did not receive.

passages.scripture: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.

lines.text: We were powerless.
We did not have the power to save ourselves.
At the right time, Christ died.
Christ died at the perfect time according to the will of God.
Christ died for the ungodly.
We were ungodly.
Christ died for us.

passages.scripture: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.

lines.text: People almost never die for a righteous man.
A righteous man does what is right.
Sometimes, for a good man, someone might dare to die.
A good man shows love, kindness and goodness.

passages.scripture: But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

lines.text: We were sinners.
We were sinners who deserved to die.
And yet, Christ died for sinners.
Christ died for us.
God proves His love for us in that Christ, the Righteous, died for us, who were unrighteous.

passages.scripture: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!

lines.text: When Jesus suffered and died, Jesus shed His blood.
Jesus shed His blood for us.
We are justified by the blood of Jesus.
The wrath of God is for godless and wicked sinners.
However, we are forgiven and justified by the blood of Christ.
Because we are forgiven and justified, we no longer deserve the wrath of God.
We will be saved from the wrath of God.
Through Jesus, we will be saved from the wrath of God.

passages.scripture: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!

lines.text: God acted when we were His enemies.
We were separated from God.
We were enemies of God.
As enemies, we were against God.
As enemies, we were separated from God.
God reconciled us to Himself.
Even though we were His enemies, God reconciled us to Himself.
God reconciled us through the death of His Son, Jesus Christ.
Now we are reconciled to God.
We are no longer enemies of God.
Now that we are reconciled to God, we will be saved.
Now reconciled, we will be saved from the wrath of God.
We will be saved through the life of Jesus Christ.

passages.scripture: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

lines.text: Also, we rejoice in God.
We rejoice in God through Jesus Christ, our Lord.
We have now received reconciliation.
Through Jesus Christ, we received reconciliation.

passages.scripture: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.

lines.text: Sin entered the world through one man.
Sin entered the world through Adam.
Adam was the first man.
Death came into the world because of sin.
All people sinned.
Therefore, death spread to all people.

passages.scripture: For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.

lines.text: Before God gave the law, sin existed in the world.
People sinned even before the law came.
If there is no law, then God does not count sin.

passages.scripture: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.

lines.text: Adam was the first man.
Moses was a leader and lawgiver.
Death ruled over people from Adam to Moses.
God gave Adam a command that Adam broke.
Adam sinned and transgressed against God.
After Adam, other people sinned.
However there were people whose sin was not like Adam.
And yet death ruled even over these people who did not sin like Adam.
Adam is a pattern of the One who was to come.

passages.scripture: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!

lines.text: Adam trespassed against the command God gave Adam.
Because of Adam's trespass, there is sin and death.
Because of Adam's trespass, many people died.
However God gives us grace.
And God gave us a gift.
The gift of God came by the grace of one Man.
This Man is Jesus Christ.
The grace of God and the gift of God overflowed to many people.
This gift of God is not like the trespass of Adam.
The grace and gift of God are much greater than the sin and death of Adam’s trespass.

passages.scripture: Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.

lines.text: One man sinned.
Adam sinned.
God gave a gift.
The gift of God is not like the result of the one man's sin.
Judgment came because of that one sin.
That judgment brought condemnation.
And later, many people trespassed.
The gift followed after these trespasses.
The gift brought justification.
Therefore, the one name's sin brought judgment and condemnation.
But the gift of God brought justification.

passages.scripture: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive an abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!

lines.text: Adam was one man.
Adam committed a trespass.
Because of Adam’s trespass, death ruled over people.
Death ruled through Adam.
Jesus Christ is one Man.
God gives an abundance of grace through Jesus Christ.
God gives the gift of righteousness through Jesus Christ.
We receive this abundant grace.
We receive this gift of righteousness.
Those who receive this grace and gift will reign in life.
We will rule in reign through Jesus Christ.

passages.scripture: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.

lines.text: Adam committed one trespass.
This one trespass brought condemnation to all people.
Jesus Christ performed one act of righteousness.
This one act brought justification to all people.
This one act brought life to all people.

passages.scripture: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.

lines.text: Adam was one man.
Adam disobeyed God.
Because Adam disobeyed, many people became sinners.
Jesus is one Man.
Jesus obeyed God.
Because Jesus obeyed, many people will become righteous.

passages.scripture: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more, so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

lines.text: God gave the law.
God gave the law so that the trespass would increase.
Sin increased because of the law.
But grace increased even more than sin.
Sin ruled over people and brought death.
Grace now rules.
Grace rules through righteousness.
Grace brings eternal life.
Jesus Christ is our Lord.
God gives eternal life through Jesus Christ.
